title: JSON
description: JSON with serde and hand-built JSON or a tiny parser
theory:
> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md). Exercise ids are shared across LEARN-* repos for cross-reference.

## JSON-shaped text

Exercises use string composition; production code would link a parser library.

exercises.title: Serialize a struct
exercises.description: `Person { Name, Age }` with `Serialize`. Build `Person { Name: "Alice", Age: 30 }`, serialize with `hand-built JSON or a tiny parser::to_string`, print it.

exercises.title: Deserialize JSON
exercises.description: Deserialize `{"Name":"Bob","Age":25}` into `Person` with `Deserialize`. Print name and age separated by a space (one line: `Bob 25`).

exercises.title: serde rename
exercises.description: `User` with C fields `first_name`, `last_name`, `birth_year` but JSON keys `first_name`, `last_name`, `birth_year` in snake_case (use `#[serde(rename = ...)]`). Marshal John/Doe/1990 and print JSON.

exercises.title: skip_serializing_if / Option
exercises.description: Model Go’s `,omitempty` with `Option` fields: only set `server: Some("api.example.com")`, leave others `None`. Serialize so output is `{"Server":"api.example.com"}` (capital `Server` to match the Go exercise).

exercises.title: Round trip
exercises.description: `Product { id, name, price }` with Serialize+Deserialize. Marshal `{1, Laptop, 999.99}`, unmarshal into a new value, print two lines exactly: `Original: {1 Laptop 999.99}` and `Recovered: {1 Laptop 999.99}` (use the same formatting for both).

exercises.title: Nested structs
exercises.description: `Address { street, city }` and `User { name, address }` with `Serialize`. Marshal and print JSON matching Go’s field names (`Street`, `City`, `Name`, `Address`).

exercises.title: Encode a slice
exercises.description: Serialize `Vec<Person>` with two entries to a JSON array string and print it (no extra spaces beyond what `hand-built JSON or a tiny parser` emits).

exercises.title: Deferred nested JSON
exercises.description: `LogEntry { level, data }` where `data` is `hand-built JSON or a tiny parser::Value`. Parse the sample, print `level` then `data` as compact JSON on the next line. (Object key order follows `hand-built JSON or a tiny parser`’s canonicalization, not the source text.)

exercises.title: Decode an array
exercises.description: Parse a JSON array of people with `hand-built JSON or a tiny parser::from_str::<Vec<Person>>`, then print each line as `Name Age` (same output as the Go decoder loop).
